description: A statement that NAMES a warehouse is refused when that warehouse is not there - live-verified, and phrased two different ways for the same missing warehouse: CREATE TASK answers "Nonexistent warehouse NOSUCH_WH was specified." while CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE and CREATE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE answer "Warehouse 'NOSUCH_WH' does not exist.", always upper-casing the name however the statement spelled it. An existing warehouse is accepted by all three, a statement with no WAREHOUSE clause is not a reference so nothing is checked, and CREATE USER ... DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE is a stored preference rather than a reference: live accepts one that does not exist, so checking it would make Frostlake stricter than Snowflake. Converted 1:1 from features/WarehouseReferenceTest (now retired); its @BeforeEach fixture is inlined per test and the account-level warehouse and user are dropped again.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE src(id INT, body VARCHAR)
CREATE TASK tk WAREHOUSE = nosuch_wh SCHEDULE = '1 minute' AS SELECT 1
CREATE TABLE src(id INT, body VARCHAR)
CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE dt TARGET_LAG = '1 hour' WAREHOUSE = nosuch_wh AS SELECT id FROM src
CREATE TABLE src(id INT, body VARCHAR)
CREATE CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE svc ON body WAREHOUSE = nosuch_wh TARGET_LAG = '1 hour' AS (SELECT id, body FROM src)
CREATE TABLE src(id INT, body VARCHAR)
CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE dt2 TARGET_LAG = '1 hour' WAREHOUSE = MiXeD_Wh AS SELECT id FROM src
CREATE TABLE src(id INT, body VARCHAR)
DROP WAREHOUSE IF EXISTS present_wh
CREATE WAREHOUSE present_wh
CREATE TASK tk WAREHOUSE = present_wh SCHEDULE = '1 minute' AS SELECT 1
CREATE DYNAMIC TABLE dt TARGET_LAG = '1 hour' WAREHOUSE = present_wh AS SELECT id FROM src
DROP WAREHOUSE present_wh
